authoring_notes.structure: 22 chapters across 9 phases. Systems-first with mathematical grounding per the README. First 3 chapters explain how an autoregressive transformer actually generates text + the KV cache memory formula + the prefill vs decode bottleneck asymmetry — these are the foundation every later chapter rests on. Frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) appear in phase 7 *after* the learner understands what PagedAttention / RadixAttention / continuous batching are solving.
authoring_notes.systems_first_rule: Per the raw-data README, the course is systems-first: chapters ch-01..ch-03 establish the generation loop + inference math + KV-cache formula. No framework-specific deep dive (vLLM/SGLang internals) before ch-16. Production reports come last (ch-20).
authoring_notes.learner_must_haves: Per the insights.md gap log, the learner explicitly flagged: vllm, sglang, pagedattention, sglang-radixattention, kv-cache-memory-formula, prefill-vs-decode, flashattention, flashattention-2, flashattention-3, flashdecoding, flashinfer. All are present and explicit chapter anchors.
authoring_notes.per_chapter_format: Each ch-XX/read.md (~200-280 lines) cites the actual loop pseudocode / KV-cache formula / scheduler policy / kernel layout from the raw-data source. ch-XX/excerpts/ contains 3-5 per-source extract files (~50-80 lines each) with verbatim equations + key code paths + key quotes. ch-XX/figures/ contains one self-contained HTML companion per chapter (inline CSS/JS, no CDN).
authoring_notes.depth_target: Foundation chapters (ch-01..ch-03) include explicit equations (attention complexity, KV-cache memory formula, prefill vs decode arithmetic intensity). Algorithm chapters include the verbatim algorithm + the exact policy/threshold/block size + at least one concrete TTFT/TPOT/throughput number from the source.
authoring_notes.framework_chapter_policy: Framework chapters (ch-16, ch-17, ch-18) are *code-level* deep dives: cite real file paths (vllm/v1/core/scheduler.py, sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py, etc.) and lift actual config knobs / API signatures. They are NOT marketing summaries.
authoring_notes.intended_format: Self-study program for someone targeting LLM serving / inference research at a frontier lab or a serving startup. Phase 1-5 give the systems foundation; phase 6 covers the inference-time acceleration literature; phase 7 grounds everything in real production stacks; phase 8 establishes the measurement vocabulary; phase 9 is hands-on.
authoring_notes.lab_paths: Lab (ch-21) and capstone (ch-22) each offer two execution paths: full-budget (H100 + Llama-3-8B, vLLM vs SGLang head-to-head) and resource-constrained (single consumer GPU + Qwen-1.8B/Llama-3.2-3B, scaled-down benchmark). Memo deliverable is the same.

tracks.title: Autoregressive Generation Loop and Inference Math
Framework Internals: vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Production Stacks

chapters.title: Autoregressive Generation Loop + Sampling
concepts: Autoregressive loop pseudocode: prompt → prefill → decode loop → stop condition; what 'one forward pass per token' actually means
Logits → probabilities → sampled token: greedy, beam, top-k, top-p (nucleus), min-p, temperature, frequency/presence penalties
Why beam search underperforms in chat (Holtzman 2019 neural-text-degeneration): degenerate repetition + low-probability surface forms
Streaming + token accounting: chunked SSE responses, finish_reason, prompt/completion token counting at the API boundary
Structured output / constrained decoding: JSON / regex / grammar finite-state masking applied to the logits

chapters.title: Transformer Inference Math: Attention Cost + MHA/MQA/GQA + RoPE
concepts: Attention complexity: O(L²·d) for prefill, O(L·d) per decode step with KV cache; the asymmetry that drives everything downstream
MHA vs MQA vs GQA: bandwidth and KV-cache memory tradeoffs; why GQA (Llama 2/3, Qwen 3) is now the default
Positional encoding for inference: RoPE rotation matrix + the inference-time context-extension consequences (YaRN, NTK-aware scaling); ALiBi as the extrapolation baseline
Per-layer per-token compute breakdown: attention vs FFN cost; why FFN dominates at small batch and attention dominates at long context
Causal mask + KV reuse: why we don't recompute past K, V at each decode step

chapters.title: KV Cache Memory Formula + Prefill vs Decode Bottlenecks
concepts: KV cache formula: bytes = 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × tokens × dtype_bytes; per-request, per-batch, per-fleet implications
Prefill is compute-bound (full attention over L tokens); decode is memory-bandwidth-bound (one token, read all KV cache); the arithmetic intensity gap
Worked example: Llama-3-70B at 8k context → ~10 GB KV per request; what this means for batch size at 80 GB H100
Static vs dynamic vs continuous batching: the three baselines that all serving systems improve on
Why decode latency is roughly KV cache size / memory bandwidth — and what every later optimization is trying to relax in this formula

chapters.title: Continuous Batching: Iteration-Level Scheduling
concepts: Static batching's problem: requests in the same batch must finish together; one long request stalls the whole batch
Orca's iteration-level scheduling + selective batching: schedule at the token-step granularity, not the request granularity
Continuous batching: at each decode step, swap in new requests and swap out finished ones; the throughput multiplier
What it gives you: 2-5× throughput at the same latency vs static batching
vLLM scheduler implementation: how WAITING / RUNNING / SWAPPED queues + priority + preemption interact

chapters.title: Chunked Prefill + Mixed-Batch Scheduling (Sarathi-Serve)
concepts: Why pure continuous batching is not enough: prefill bursts (big compute) stall decode tokens (latency-sensitive)
Chunked prefill: split a long prefill into smaller chunks and interleave them with decode steps
Mixed-batch scheduling: a single forward pass contains both prefill chunks and decode tokens, balanced against the GPU's compute capacity
Configuration knobs: max_num_batched_tokens, max_chunk_size; how to tune them
Effect on TTFT vs TPOT: TTFT goes up slightly, TPOT goes down significantly, total throughput rises

chapters.title: PagedAttention + Block-Based KV Cache (vLLM)
concepts: The fragmentation problem: contiguous per-request KV cache wastes memory at the end of each sequence and during preemption
Virtual-memory analogy: PagedAttention splits KV cache into fixed-size blocks (typically 16 tokens) and maintains a per-sequence block table
Memory utilization: PagedAttention's headline 96 % utilization vs ~60 % for naive contiguous allocation
Copy-on-write for parallel sampling / beam search: same block shared across siblings until divergence
PagedAttention kernel: how the attention computation indexes through block tables at runtime

chapters.title: Prefix Caching + RadixAttention (SGLang)
concepts: Prefix caching: shared system prompts / few-shot exemplars / system instructions across many requests — recompute or reuse?
vLLM's APC (Automatic Prefix Cache): hash-based block matching + LRU eviction
SGLang's RadixAttention: store KV blocks in a radix tree keyed by token sequences; automatic matching of any prefix prefix
Hit rates in practice: 50-90 % for chat workloads with fixed system prompts; 20-50 % for arbitrary user prompts
Hierarchical cache (SGLang HiCache): GPU → CPU → distributed storage tiers; eviction across tiers

chapters.title: KV Cache Compression + Eviction (H2O / SnapKV / Attention Sinks / Quest)
concepts: Heavy-Hitter Oracle (H2O): a small fraction of past tokens dominate attention weight; evict the rest
SnapKV observation window: use the last few tokens' attention patterns to decide which past tokens to keep
Attention Sinks (Streaming LLM): keep the first N tokens always; they act as soft attention anchors
Quest query-aware sparsity: at decode time, fetch only the KV pages relevant to the current query
InfLLM long-context inference: external memory + cached-block reuse for million-token context

chapters.title: Prefill/Decode Disaggregation (DistServe / Splitwise / Mooncake)
concepts: Why prefill and decode interfere even with chunked prefill: different ideal batch sizes, different memory needs, different SLO targets
Disaggregation: dedicate one pool of GPUs to prefill, another to decode; ship KV cache between them
DistServe's TTFT vs TPOT tradeoff: optimize each pool independently
Splitwise + Mooncake: KV-cache-centric serving architecture; cross-pool RDMA / NVLink KV transfer
When disaggregation pays off (high QPS, mixed long+short requests) vs when it doesn't (uniform short requests)

chapters.title: Admission Control + Goodput + Fair Scheduling (VTC / Niyama / SLO)
concepts: Throughput vs goodput: throughput counts all completed requests; goodput counts only those meeting their SLO
Admission control: reject incoming requests if you can predict you can't meet their SLO; saves resources for in-flight requests
Fair scheduling — Virtual Token Counter (VTC): give each user their fair share of tokens; the LLM-serving equivalent of fair queueing
Niyama QoS-driven scheduling: separate interactive (low-TPOT) and batch (high-throughput) tiers
The 2026 trend: serving needs mathematical optimization, not heuristics; mixed-integer scheduling formulations starting to appear

chapters.title: FlashAttention Lineage (1/2/3 + FlashDecoding + FlashInfer)
concepts: FlashAttention 1 (Dao 2022): IO-aware tiling — avoid materializing the L×L attention matrix in HBM; everything stays in SRAM
FlashAttention 2 (Dao 2023): better work partitioning + lower non-matmul FLOPs; 2× faster than FA1
FlashAttention 3 (2024): Hopper-era asynchronous + FP8 attention; ping-pong pipelining + WGMMA
FlashDecoding: split-K decoding for long-context; parallelize the KV-cache scan across multiple SMs
FlashInfer: serving-system-aware kernel library; paged attention + cascade attention + prefix-shared kernels

chapters.title: CUDA Graphs + Runtime Optimizations
concepts: Launch overhead: ~10 µs per kernel; with ~80 layers × 10 kernels/layer, decode latency is half kernel launches
CUDA Graphs: capture a static graph of kernel invocations, replay with one launch — eliminates the overhead
The 'static shape' constraint: graph capture requires fixed batch size, sequence length, etc.; serving needs piecewise capture
Frameworks' approach: vLLM piecewise CUDA graphs (one graph per discrete batch-size bucket); TensorRT-LLM ahead-of-time engine build
Other runtime wins: NCCL collective fusion, kernel fusion, dynamic-shape JIT

chapters.title: Parallel Inference: Tensor / Pipeline / Expert Parallel
concepts: Tensor parallelism for inference: split QKV/FFN matrices across GPUs; all-reduce after each matmul; what overhead this adds
Pipeline parallelism for inference: split layers across GPUs; microbatching; the bubble cost
Expert parallelism for MoE inference: route each token to expert GPUs; the all-to-all collective
Combined: TP×PP×EP for frontier MoE models (DeepSeek V3 671B, Mixtral 8x7B/8x22B); when each helps
Communication patterns: NCCL all-reduce vs all-to-all; intra-node NVLink vs inter-node InfiniBand

chapters.title: Speculative Decoding Foundations
concepts: The core idea: a small draft model proposes K tokens; the target model verifies them in one forward pass
Speculative sampling rule (Chen et al.): accept token if u ≤ p_target(x) / p_draft(x); otherwise reject and resample from the residual distribution
Why it preserves the target distribution exactly (no quality loss)
Speedup math: expected acceptance rate α × (K speedup) − overhead; typical 1.5-3× speedup
Choice of draft model: smaller LLM (Llama-2-7B as draft for Llama-2-70B) vs distilled draft vs n-gram speculation

chapters.title: Multi-Head + Feature-Level + N-Gram Draft Methods (Medusa / EAGLE / Lookahead / PLD / MTP)
concepts: Medusa: multiple decoding heads on the target model itself; draft + verify in a single forward pass — no separate draft model needed
EAGLE / EAGLE-2: feature-level draft (operates on hidden states, not tokens); dynamic draft tree; 3-4× speedup
Lookahead Decoding: Jacobi-style parallel n-gram generation; no draft model required
Prompt Lookup Decoding (PLD): if a draft token already appears in the prompt, use it directly; nearly-free speedup for RAG / code completion
Multi-Token Prediction heads: train the model to predict K tokens at once (DeepSeek V3 used this for native speculative decoding)

chapters.title: vLLM Internals: Scheduler + Cache Manager + Structured Output
concepts: Architecture overview: API server → engine → scheduler → model executor → worker; what runs where
Scheduler internals: WAITING / RUNNING / SWAPPED queues; iteration-level scheduling loop; chunked prefill integration
Block manager: free-block pool, block tables per sequence, copy-on-write for parallel sampling, APC prefix cache integration
Structured output backend: outlines / xgrammar integration; guided JSON / regex / EBNF
Production knobs: max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens, gpu_memory_utilization, swap_space, prefix-caching enable

chapters.title: SGLang Internals: RadixAttention + HiCache + Frontend Language
concepts: Architecture overview: frontend (Python DSL with gen / select / fork) → runtime → RadixAttention-aware scheduler → backend
Frontend language: parallel + nested LLM calls expressed as a coroutine-style DSL; the cross-call prefix-reuse value prop
RadixAttention end-to-end: tree structure → prefix matching → KV-block reuse → LRU eviction
HiCache: GPU → CPU → distributed storage tiers; per-tier hit-rate measurement; offload bandwidth as a bottleneck
Structured output: grammar-guided decoding integrated with prefix cache

chapters.title: Production Serving Stacks: TensorRT-LLM, TGI, LightLLM, LMDeploy, DeepSpeed-FastGen, llama.cpp
concepts: TensorRT-LLM: ahead-of-time engine build, paged KV, inflight batching, FP8/NVFP4 path, Triton integration
HF TGI: router + shards, Rust frontend, integration with Transformers, focus on production deployment ergonomics
LightLLM / LMDeploy / DeepSpeed-FastGen: per-architecture engineering choices; what they do better/worse than vLLM
llama.cpp / llama-server: CPU + Apple-Silicon-first; gguf integration; slot-based batching
Choose-by-workload rubric: who picks what and why (vLLM for OSS flexibility, TensorRT-LLM for NVIDIA-only max-perf, SGLang for prefix-heavy workloads, llama.cpp for edge)

chapters.title: Inference Benchmarks + Metrics (TTFT / TPOT / ITL / Goodput)
concepts: The four core metrics: TTFT (time to first token), TPOT (time per output token), ITL (inter-token latency), throughput (tokens/sec); when each one matters
Common traps: percentile lies (p50 looks good, p99 disasters), warm-up cache contamination, request-rate sweeps that miss the saturation point
Workload design: ShareGPT-style synthetic traces; request length distributions; request-rate sweeps
Benchmark stacks: GenAI-Perf (NVIDIA), LLMPerf (Anyscale), MLPerf Inference LLM, HELM, vLLM/SGLang built-in benchmarks
Goodput under SLO: the metric that actually matches business value; how to define your SLO and report goodput correctly

chapters.title: Production Model Inference Reports: Llama 3 / Qwen 3 / DeepSeek V3+R1 / GPT-OSS / Mixtral / Gemma
concepts: Llama 3: GQA-8 (Llama-3-8B) / GQA-128 (70B); 128k context; tokenizer + chat-template gotchas
Qwen 3: hybrid thinking/non-thinking; MoE 30B/235B; YaRN context scaling; serving implications
DeepSeek V3: 671B MoE, 37B active, MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) compressing KV; FP8 deployment
DeepSeek R1: long-CoT generation patterns; sampling and serving implications (max_tokens, finish_reason, latency budget)
GPT-OSS, Mixtral, Gemma, Phi: representative serving cases — MXFP4 MoE, sparse routing, edge inference, small-model local

chapters.title: Lab — Deploy + Benchmark vLLM vs SGLang Head-to-Head
concepts: Full-budget path: H100 + Llama-3-8B-Instruct; deploy vLLM and SGLang side-by-side; run ShareGPT request-rate sweep (1 → 32 req/s) and capture TTFT / TPOT / throughput / goodput@p99
Resource-constrained path: single 24 GB GPU + Qwen-1.8B; same benchmarks at smaller scale
Required ablation: enable/disable prefix caching, vary max_num_batched_tokens, vary chunked-prefill chunk_size; report effect
Memo deliverable: side-by-side TTFT / TPOT / throughput / goodput table at 3 saturation points; which framework wins for which workload and why
Reflection: under what circumstances would your conclusion flip (longer context, more prefix sharing, lower SLO)?

chapters.title: Capstone — Reproduce a Serving Optimization From Scratch
concepts: Pick one of {PagedAttention, RadixAttention, Speculative Decoding, EAGLE, Disaggregated Prefill/Decode}; implement from the paper (no copy-paste from author repo)

Full-budget path: H100 + Llama-3-8B; reproduce the paper's headline number (PagedAttention 96% utilization, RadixAttention 5× throughput on shared-prefix workloads, Speculative Decoding 2-3× TPOT speedup, EAGLE 3× TPOT speedup, DistServe N% goodput improvement)
Resource-constrained path: single 24 GB GPU + Qwen-1.8B; reproduce the qualitative result if you can't match the absolute number
Reproduction memo: did you match within 10 %? If not, where is the gap (hardware, batch size, dataset, hyperparameter)?
Optional stretch: PR your implementation to vLLM or SGLang as a draft contribution
